title: Phase 3: Session-Level Durability for Cognitive Router
description: Implement session-level durability mechanisms to prevent single model failures from aborting entire cron jobs or agent sessions. This involves adding an abort feedback loop, session-level fallback chains, idle timeout/stall detection, and a cron-specific routing profile.
goal_statement: Make the Cognitive Router durable enough that a single slow or hung model cannot kill an entire cron job or agent session, by adding abort feedback loops, session-level fallback chains, proactive stall detection, and cron-optimized routing profiles.

steps.title: Update database schema for abort events
steps.description: Modify the SQLite database schema in db_service.ts to include a new table for storing abort events (provider, model, turnsCompleted, durationMs, sessionKey). Create a migration script if necessary or handle schema creation on startup.
steps.intended_outcome: Database schema supports recording abort events with all required fields, and the application starts successfully with the updated schema.

steps.title: Implement POST /v1/report/abort endpoint
steps.description: Add the POST /v1/report/abort endpoint to server.ts. Validate the request body {provider, model, turnsCompleted, durationMs, sessionKey}. Call a new method in cost_tracker.ts to record the abort event and update reliability scores.
steps.intended_outcome: The endpoint accepts valid abort reports, persists them to the database, and triggers the cost tracker update logic.

steps.title: Update cost tracker for abort penalties
steps.description: Modify cost_tracker.ts to handle abort events. Implement logic to decrement the reliability score for the specific provider/model by at least 0.2 per event. Ensure this state is persisted and affects subsequent routing decisions.
steps.intended_outcome: Reported aborts result in a measurable reduction (>= 0.2) of the offending model's reliability score in the cost tracker.

steps.title: Implement GET /v1/fallback endpoint
steps.description: Add the GET /v1/fallback endpoint to server.ts. It should accept query parameters provider, model, turn, and reason. It calls router.ts to find the next-best candidate excluding the failed one.
steps.intended_outcome: The endpoint returns a JSON response with the next best candidate and rationale, ensuring the failed provider/model is excluded.

steps.title: Implement mid-stream stall detection
steps.description: Modify proxy-stream.ts to detect stalled connections. Use the ROUTER_STREAM_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS configuration. If no data is received within the timeout, abort the request and mark the connection as a zombie.
steps.intended_outcome: Active streams that idle for longer than ROUTER_STREAM_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS are aborted and tagged as zombies.

steps.title: Update cost tracker zombie pattern flags
steps.description: Enhance cost_tracker.ts to track zombie connection patterns per provider/model. If a model accumulates 3+ zombie stalls, automatically set the unstable or contextLimited flag.
steps.intended_outcome: Models causing frequent stalls are flagged as unstable or contextLimited in the cost tracker.

steps.title: Implement cron-specific routing profile
steps.description: Update router.ts to accept an optional routingProfile parameter in decide(). If profile is 'cron', adjust the scoring algorithm to weigh proven completion rates higher than raw capability. Update cost_tracker to track completion rates per model/intent.
steps.intended_outcome: The decide() function supports a 'cron' profile that prioritizes reliable models over theoretically capable ones.

steps.title: Write integration tests for new features
steps.description: Create tests in the tests/ directory covering: the abort endpoint writing to DB, reliability score reduction, fallback endpoint selection, stall detection timeouts, zombie flagging, and cron profile selection.
steps.intended_outcome: All new functionality is covered by automated tests that verify the specific success criteria.

steps.title: Run full test suite and verify compatibility
steps.description: Run npm test to ensure all existing Phase 1+2 tests pass and the new tests pass. Verify that the application builds correctly with tsc.
steps.intended_outcome: All tests pass, the build succeeds, and no existing functionality is broken.

assumptions: The existing SQLite database setup in db_service.ts is accessible and writable.
ROUTER_STREAM_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS is defined in the configuration.
The project environment has Node.js and npm installed.
Existing cost_tracker metrics infrastructure can be extended without major refactoring.
risks: Modifying the database schema on a live system could cause downtime if not handled carefully.
Aggressive reliability score reduction (0.2) might unfairly deprioritize a generally good model that had a transient issue.
Stall detection logic might mistakenly abort long-running valid computations if the timeout is too aggressive.
Adding new parameters to decide() might break compatibility with existing clients not expecting them (though it is optional).
success_criteria: POST /v1/report/abort endpoint exists and writes abort events to SQLite with provider, model, turnsCompleted, durationMs, sessionKey fields
GET /v1/fallback endpoint returns next-best candidate excluding the failed provider/model, with rationale
Abort events reduce reliability score for the reported provider+model by at least 0.2 per event
Mid-stream stall detection aborts zombie connections after configurable idle period (ROUTER_STREAM_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS already exists at 45s default)
Zombie connection tracking feeds into cost_tracker pattern flags — 3+ zombie stalls set unstable or contextLimited flag
decide() accepts optional routingProfile parameter; 'cron' profile biases scoring toward models with proven completion rates over raw capability
New tests cover abort feedback, fallback chain, stall detection, and cron profile selection
